title: interactive-session-slope-calcs
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad to think about session-based credits that tilt pricing for short interactive UIs (chatbots, assistants) vs. long-context analytic sessions. Not final — just trying to get slopes and anchors that roughly match token-driven unit economics while keeping UX friction low.

Notes / assumptions (rough):
- Baseline infra assumption: amortized GPU-hour cost for inference stack = $2.40/hr (mix of reserved + infra overhead). This is the backend marginal cost we use for token math.
- Serving throughput (avg observed): 120 tokens/sec per GPU for mid-sized 7–13B-class quantized runtime under our batching regime. (varies by seq length & batch).
- Effective tokens/hr per GPU = 120 * 3600 = 432k tokens/hr. => cost per token = $2.40 / 432k = ~$0.00000556/token (~5.6e-6).
- Add fixed infra + ops overhead to get platform marginal cost per token ~ 1.5x => ~$8.4e-6/token. Round to 8.5e-6 for safety.

Session model: credit per session = base_overhead + slope * expected_session_tokens.
- base_overhead (session start/setup & KV/cache warmup) estimate = 50 tokens equivalent (fast warmup).
- slope = 1 x token cost for predictable per-token runtime consumption. But for UX small sessions we can subsidize first N tokens.

Quick anchors (toy):
- Micro session (short chat widget): expected 200 tokens/session (user prompt+model reply+context).
  - raw token cost = 200 * 8.5e-6 = $0.0017. + base_overhead (50 tokens => $0.000425). Total marginal cost ~= $0.002125/session.
  - Consider selling Micro pack: 1000 sessions = cost to us ~$2.125. List price per 1k = $10 (for PLG / lowest tier) => margin ~78%.

- Standard session (utility assistant): expected 1,000 tokens/session.
  - raw token cost = 1000 * 8.5e-6 = $0.0085. + base_overhead $0.000425 => $0.008925 ~ $0.009/session.
  - 1k sessions = cost ~$9 => list price per 1k sessions = $35 (mid) => margin 74%.

- Analytic session (long context / 32k): expected 10k tokens/session.
  - raw token cost = 10k * 8.5e-6 = $0.085. + base $0.000425 => $0.0854/session.
  - 1k sessions cost ~$85 => list price 1k = $220 => margin ~61%.

Observations: margins look healthy at modest markups. But heavy tail of very long sessions can blow up cost quickly. Need protections: quota cap, overage price, auto-truncate or downsample context.

Slope experiment idea (tiering):
- Offer two metering primitives: session-credit and token-bucket. Session-credit = buys you a session with an expected token budget; token-bucket is pure tokens. Map session-credits -> token budgets with decreasing marginal price for very long budgets.
- Pricing curve example: 
  - session-credit S1 (micro): includes 300 tokens equivalent. Price = $0.01 per credit. (cost to us ~ $0.0025).
  - session-credit S2 (standard): 1k tokens. Price = $0.03 per credit.
  - session-credit S3 (long): 10k tokens. Price = $0.20 per credit.
Rationale: S3 discounted per-token vs S2 to reflect that long sessions are rarer and buyers expect bulk trade-offs. But still need safeguards (burst caps, async batch pricing)

Back-of-envelope: per-session price->effective per-token (examples):
- S1: $0.01 / 300 = $3.33e-5 per token vs our ~8.5e-6 => markup ~3.9x.
- S2: $0.03 / 1000 = $3e-5 per token => ~3.5x markup.
- S3: $0.20 / 10k = $2e-5 per token => ~2.35x markup.

Edge cases & behavioral considerations:
- Very short micro bursts (<= 30 tokens) — users hate paying for small token budgets. Add rounding rule: sessions < 50 tokens cost the same as 50-token micro-credit (we already subsidize base).
- Idle chat sessions (users open tab, no activity) consume KV memory but not tokens — include an idle timeout metric (free up cache after X minutes). Charge only on server-side forwards.
- Rewrites / retries: multiple model calls inside a session (tool calls) should either be charged separately or consumed from a larger session bucket. Need to avoid double-billing surprises.

Open calc variants to try next:
1) Use conservative GPU throughput (80 t/s) and recalc per-token cost. (downside: increases list price significantly)
2) Add network egress & KMS overhead per session (flat $0.0005 est) and see effect on micro tier economics.
3) Simulate percentile profile of sessions (p10,p50,p90,p99) and compute expected cost under each tier mapping.

Customer-facing wording ideas (short):
- "Interactive Credits" — buy credits that map to sessions. Credits redeem for sessions of different sizes. Simple UX: one SKU for micro (button/chat), one for pro (agent workflows), one for analytics (long context).
- Display: "This chat uses 180 tokens — 1 micro credit used (300 tokens)" + show percent remaining in the credit.

Questions / TODOs:
- Get real telemetry: distribution of session token counts (histogram), median session length, 95th percentile. (SRE / product analytics).
- Validate GPU tokens/sec under representative customer workloads (SLA vs median). Tag models: 7B vs 13B vs Llama2-70B — need model-class multipliers.
- Decide on overage behavior: block vs charge per-token post-credit? (UX tradeoff).
- Draft small experiment: convert 10k existing free-tier sessions to micro-credit model, measure conversion and user complaints.

Random side-notes:
- Could introduce a tiny recurring subscription that provides credit top-up + lower per-unit price for high-velocity customers (combo: seat+credits).
- For enterprise: commit to monthly credit pool with rollover & custom overage pricing; provide tools to pin model variants for cheaper inference.

Bottom line: session-credit slope feels promising — keeps UX simple for chat while still maintaining token-aligned unit economics. Need telemetry + a couple conservative re-runs with different throughput assumptions before proposing pricing decks.

-- Ava

(quick changes: if we assume amortized GPU cost = $4/hr, per-token cost doubles -> micro 1k price needs bump to keep margin)
